In [[mathematics]], a '''hyper-finite field''' is an [[uncountable set|uncountable]] [[field (mathematics)|field]] similar in many ways to [[finite field]]s. More precisely a field ''F'' is called hyper-finite if it is uncountable and [[quasi-finite field|quasi-finite]], and for every subfield ''E'', every absolutely entire ''E''-algebra ([[regular field extension]] of ''E'')  of smaller [[cardinality]] than ''F'' can be embedded in ''F''. They were introduced by {{harvtxt|Ax|1968}}. Every hyper-finite field is a [[pseudo-finite field]], and is in particular a model for the first-order theory of finite fields.
